summary: Session-resume cache drift causing p95 generation latency and streaming disconnects on repeated conversational turns
description: Issue summary: Since 2026-03-11 ~18:00 UTC NimbusPay started reporting repeat-turn responses are taking 2-3x longer (p95) and some streaming sessions terminate with protocol-level disconnects after emitting 0-3 tokens. Impact: Customer-facing chat UI experiences intermittent stalls and session disconnects for returning conversational turns; revenue-impacting for high-frequency users. Environment: prod (us-east) using dedicated capacity, customers pinned to redwood-v1-chat. Observed: p95 generation latency increased from ~120ms to ~340ms for repeat prompts; streaming socket resets seen in gateway logs corresponding to 504/502 from serving nodes. Hypothesis: session-resume (prefix) cache entries are occasionally resolved against stale shard index leading to fallback cold-path reads and duplicated KV fetches, amplifying latency and causing partial stream writes then disconnect on retry. This ticket captures the customer report, initial triage, investigation, and proposed mitigations.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use NimbusPay account with a conversation that has a cached session prefix (repeat prompt scenario).
2) Issue identical follow-up prompt within 5-30s of prior turn to exercise session-resume path.
3) Observe p95 token generation latency in console or via customer SDK metrics; optionally enable streaming to see disconnects.
4) Compare behavior against pinned older model variant (if available) to rule out model-side perf regressions.
logs_and_metrics: Gateway logs: client_stream_id=cnv-93a2 saw upstream 502 then socket reset at token 2
Console trace: request_id=rn-7f12 prefix_lookup fallback_path=true kv_read_count=3
Alert: infra-monitoring.p95_generation_latency exceeded threshold (200ms) for redwood-v1-chat between 18:00-19:30 UTC
comments: 2026-03-12 09:12 - Support (Aisha): Opened ticket after NimbusPay reported repeated stalls. Collected initial logs, sample request IDs, and reproduction steps from customer. Customer notes problem started after a small rolling change on 2026-03-11.

2026-03-12 10:03 - SRE (Tomás): Correlated customer request IDs with serving traces. Noted increased prefix fallback to cold KV path and duplicated KV fetches for same session key. Added label kvcache-drift.

2026-03-12 11:45 - Eng (Marta): Looked at kvcatalog reindex job; found an overlapping reindex window that could cause short-lived shard mapping inconsistencies during live rollouts. Created INT-1102 to track reindex fix and safe rollout gating.

2026-03-13 07:56 - Support (Aisha): Customer confirms mitigation attempt by pinning model to earlier variant gave reduced latency but did not eliminate disconnects. Customer requested ETA for a permanent fix.

2026-03-13 15:20 - SRE (Tomás): Applied a conservative hotfix: disable speculative prefetch for session-resume on affected fleet in us-east. Observed immediate reduction in KV read duplicates and p95 downsampled by ~30% for sampled requests. Monitoring continues.
2026-03-14 08:40 - Eng (Marta): Draft PR created to add reindex epoch checks and leader fencing to kvcatalog reindex operator (PR linked). Planning canary rollout after QA.
2026-03-14 12:01 - Support (Aisha): Notified customer of ongoing mitigation and follow-up plan; they requested we keep ticket open until canary completes.
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: model degradation — rejected after comparing pinned variant, which improved but did not resolve streaming resets.
Metric dive shows correlated spikes in kv_read_count and prefix_fallback_rate exactly when p95 increased.

kvcatalog reindex overlap discovered: two reindex workers briefly produced inconsistent shard maps leading to 'prefix->shard' resolution race where some serving nodes still used old map while others used new map.

Race leads to duplicated prefetches: serving node A issues prefetch to shard X while node B redirects to shard Y; the fallback path triggers synchronous cold reads and additional locks, amplifying tail latency.
Streaming disconnect rationale: partial tokens emitted while backend experiences increased latency then upstream gateway sees deadline/504 and tears down socket leading to observed resets.
Repro attempt: created local harness replaying sample request IDs; toggling reindex produced repeatable p95 increase ~2.2x during overlap window.
resolution: Workaround applied: speculative prefetch for session-resume disabled in us-east fleet (hotfix) — immediate p95 improvement seen. Workaround status: Active.
Planned fix: deploy kvcatalog reindex operator changes (leader fencing + epoch check) from PR #4121; will canary in us-east on 2026-03-16 then expand if stable.
Follow-up actions: add a dashboard for prefix-map-sync-lag, create an alert for reindex overlap, add postmortem runbook steps and customer communication template.
Customer communication: notified NimbusPay of workaround and timeline; will keep ticket open until canary completes and customer verifies resolution in their workload.
If canary shows regression, rollback path: re-enable speculative prefetch with additional dedupe gate and consult datastore team for alternative safe reindex strategies.
